scope: Theorem 2.2 (Boundary flux and strip mass) of the manuscript “Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length honeycomb walks” (preprints/Mass-and-covering-exponents-for-fixed-length-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 58011713f8bb7cd5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every finite simply connected union D of triangular tiles with simple polygonal boundary and each boundary source port a, ∑︂ b∈∂D ∑︂ γ:a→b ρ|γ| e3iW(γ)/8 = 1, where W is total signed turning from the initial inward direction to the final outward direction. If D is convex, its unsigned exit mass is at most 1/c. For each h ≥ 1, all strip sums defined above are finite and cAh + Bh = 1, Bh+1 ≤ Bh, Bh ≍ (1 + h)−1/4 , mh ≍ h3/4 , mh+1 − mh ≍ Bh. The constants are independent of h, and bh(x) = bh(−x).
